readerQuestion: How can I tidy Home Assistant device and dashboard names without breaking the entity references my automations use?
directAnswer: Change a card name for one dashboard or a device/entity name for broader display wording, preserving working entity IDs. Before device/entity renames, inspect name-dependent templates and state triggers that can react to attribute-only changes. Start with two temperature cards that share one sensor; deliberately changing an ID requires repairing references.
originalContribution: Sections 1–3 provide a reversible two-card temperature exercise, explicit information-only tap actions, and a worked S-04 sensor audit table separating physical inventory, room, device name, entity function, entity ID and card title. The expected results distinguish a visual change from a reference change. Section 4 and the troubleshooting table map missing references, duplicated names, absent unique IDs and custom-card differences to different next steps.
limitations: Documentation research and local website verification only. No live Home Assistant configuration or physical device was tested, and the illustrative sensor is not a Tara installation. The generated cover is labeled as illustration. 2026.11-specific contextual naming and Main entity settings are identified; older versions and third-party card behavior can differ. The workflow does not promise a complete automatic audit of external tools, name-based templates or historical database continuity after an ID migration.
proofreadFixes: The final automated proofreading pass added the important attribute-trigger caveat before any device rename and to the TLDR: preserving an entity ID does not prevent a state trigger reacting to a changed friendly_name attribute. Limited the device exercise to non-critical monitoring and retained a card-only starting test. Replaced an awkward exact-query opening with plain prose. Added a swipe hint to the worked-example table, changed its heading to avoid an awkward mobile break, and gave the YAML block a readable background, padding and horizontal scrolling. Checked that both card tap actions open information, that a fixed card title does not become a universal entity name, that automatic-dashboard takeover has a consequence, and that friendly_name is retained for compatibility rather than already removed. Rechecked the corrected page and library cards visually. No human or expert review is claimed.

claimChecks.claim: Entity name and entity ID are separate settings. Changing the name does not change its ID; manual ID changes require reviewing automation and script references. Recreate entity IDs generates IDs rather than changing display names.
The 2026.11 naming migration retains existing IDs, adds contextual display names, retains friendly_name for compatibility, and can make custom cards or name-based templates display different wording.
A card name can be a static string or composed name parts. A card-specific title does not rename the underlying entity or other cards.

The Tile example uses the documented entity, name, tap_action and icon_tap_action fields. Taking control of an automatically managed dashboard stops automatic updates, so the exercise uses an already manually managed dashboard.

A state trigger without From/To restrictions also reacts to attribute-only changes; a name change affecting friendly_name can therefore matter even when its ID stays unchanged. The reader must audit such dependencies before the device-name exercise.

An internal unique ID differs from an entity ID; absent unique IDs can limit UI editing. Adding one depends on the integration, and a reader should not invent a replacement registry identifier to fix a display name.
Old entity references can remain after an ID rename. Repair affected triggers, conditions and actions instead of resetting or re-pairing working hardware, and review other references separately.
Settings > Tools > States displays the entity state and descriptive attributes. The verification is read-only and does not instruct the reader to use Set state or actuate critical equipment.

Main entity of the device uses the device name for the main function; it is not a reason to give every measurement the same name. Entity ID format affects newly generated IDs and some integrations supply their own suggestions.
